# The Component Kernel of a Finite Simple Graph

This file gives a fully type-checking foundational formalization of the
*component-kernel theorem* for finite simple graphs over `ℝ`, together with a
small collection of "modular signature" corollaries.

## Mathematical content

Given a finite simple graph `G : SimpleGraph V`, view the functions `V → ℝ` as a
real vector space.  The **harmonic kernel** `harmonicKernel G` is the subspace of
functions that are constant across every edge:

  `f ∈ harmonicKernel G ↔ ∀ {u v}, G.Adj u v → f u = f v`.

Such functions are exactly the functions that are *locally constant* with respect
to the graph: they are constant along every walk and hence on every connected
component.  Consequently the harmonic kernel is naturally isomorphic, as a real
vector space, to the space of functions on the set of connected components:

  `harmonicKernel G ≃ₗ[ℝ] (G.ConnectedComponent → ℝ)`.

Taking dimensions yields the central result, that the dimension of the harmonic
kernel equals the number of connected components:

  `specModSig G = Fintype.card G.ConnectedComponent`.

We call `specModSig G := Module.finrank ℝ (harmonicKernel G)` the **spectral
modular signature** of `G`.  (Up to the usual identification of the harmonic
kernel with the kernel of the combinatorial graph Laplacian, this is the
nullity of the Laplacian; we do *not* prove that matrix identity here — the
deliverable is the purely component-theoretic statement.)

## Main results

* `harmonicKernel_walk` / `harmonicKernel_reachable` — kernel elements are
  constant along walks and on reachable pairs.
* `harmonicKernelEquiv` — the linear equivalence with component-functions.
* `specModSig_eq_card_components` — the component-kernel theorem.
* `specModSig_pos` — the signature is positive when `V` is nonempty.
* `specModSig_le_card` — the signature is at most `Fintype.card V`.
* `connected_iff_specModSig_eq_one` — connectivity is `signature = 1`.
* `specModSig_iso` — isomorphic graphs have equal signatures.
* `specModSig_eq_card_iff_edgeless` — the signature is maximal iff the graph is
  edgeless.

## Scope

This file makes **no** empirical claim about the lengths of Lean/Coq/Isabelle
proofs and proves **no** asymptotic proof-difficulty conjecture.  It isolates the
rigorous finite-dimensional linear-algebra core on which such a theory could be
built.
-/

import Mathlib

open SimpleGraph

namespace SpectralProofSignature

variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)

/-! ## The harmonic kernel -/

/-- The **harmonic kernel** of a graph: the subspace of real-valued vertex
functions that are constant across every edge. -/
def harmonicKernel (G : SimpleGraph V) : Submodule ℝ (V → ℝ) where
  carrier := {f | ∀ ⦃u v : V⦄, G.Adj u v → f u = f v}
  add_mem' {a b} ha hb := by intro u v h; simp [ha h, hb h]
  zero_mem' := by intro u v h; rfl
  smul_mem' c a ha := by intro u v h; simp [ha h]

@[simp] lemma mem_harmonicKernel_iff {f : V → ℝ} :
    f ∈ harmonicKernel G ↔ ∀ ⦃u v : V⦄, G.Adj u v → f u = f v := Iff.rfl

/-- A harmonic kernel element is constant along every walk. -/
lemma harmonicKernel_walk {f : V → ℝ} (hf : f ∈ harmonicKernel G) :
    ∀ {u v : V} (_ : G.Walk u v), f u = f v := by
  intro u v p
  induction p with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons h _ ih => exact (hf h).trans ih

/-- A harmonic kernel element is constant on every reachable pair of vertices. -/
lemma harmonicKernel_reachable {f : V → ℝ} (hf : f ∈ harmonicKernel G)
    {u v : V} (h : G.Reachable u v) : f u = f v := by
  obtain ⟨p⟩ := h
  exact harmonicKernel_walk G hf p

/-- Membership in the harmonic kernel is *equivalent* to being constant on every
reachable pair of vertices (not merely on adjacent ones). -/
lemma mem_harmonicKernel_iff_reachable {f : V → ℝ} :
    f ∈ harmonicKernel G ↔ ∀ ⦃u v : V⦄, G.Reachable u v → f u = f v := by
  constructor
  · intro hf u v h; exact harmonicKernel_reachable G hf h
  · intro hf u v h; exact hf h.reachable

/-! ## The component-function equivalence -/

variable [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableRel G.Adj]

/-- The forward map: a harmonic kernel element descends to a function on the set
of connected components, by evaluation at any representative vertex. -/
noncomputable def toComp : harmonicKernel G →ₗ[ℝ] (G.ConnectedComponent → ℝ) where
  toFun f := ConnectedComponent.lift f.1 (fun _ _ p _ => harmonicKernel_walk G f.2 p)
  map_add' f g := by funext c; induction c using ConnectedComponent.ind; rfl
  map_smul' c f := by funext x; induction x using ConnectedComponent.ind; rfl

/-- The backward map: a function on connected components pulls back to a vertex
function (which is automatically harmonic). -/
def fromComp : (G.ConnectedComponent → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] harmonicKernel G where
  toFun g := ⟨fun v => g (G.connectedComponentMk v), by
    intro u v h
    show g (G.connectedComponentMk u) = g (G.connectedComponentMk v)
    rw [ConnectedComponent.connectedComponentMk_eq_of_adj h]⟩
  map_add' g h := by ext v; rfl
  map_smul' c g := by ext v; rfl

/-- The harmonic kernel of `G` is linearly equivalent to the space of functions
on the connected components of `G`. -/
noncomputable def harmonicKernelEquiv :
    harmonicKernel G ≃ₗ[ℝ] (G.ConnectedComponent → ℝ) :=
  LinearEquiv.ofLinear (toComp G) (fromComp G)
    (by ext g c; induction c using ConnectedComponent.ind; rfl)
    (by ext f v; rfl)

/-! ## The spectral modular signature -/

/-- The **spectral modular signature** of `G`: the dimension of its harmonic
kernel as a real vector space. -/
noncomputable def specModSig (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank ℝ (harmonicKernel G)

/-- **Component-kernel theorem.** The spectral modular signature equals the number
of connected components. -/
theorem specModSig_eq_card_components :
    specModSig G = Fintype.card G.ConnectedComponent := by
  rw [specModSig, (harmonicKernelEquiv G).finrank_eq, Module.finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card]

/-! ## Corollaries -/

omit [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [DecidableRel G.Adj] in
/-- The connected-component projection is surjective. -/
lemma connectedComponentMk_surjective :
    Function.Surjective G.connectedComponentMk := by
  intro c
  induction c using ConnectedComponent.ind with
  | _ v => exact ⟨v, rfl⟩

/-- For a nonempty vertex set the signature is positive. -/
theorem specModSig_pos [Nonempty V] : 0 < specModSig G := by
  rw [specModSig_eq_card_components]
  have : Nonempty G.ConnectedComponent := ⟨G.connectedComponentMk (Classical.arbitrary V)⟩
  exact Fintype.card_pos

/-- The signature is bounded above by the number of vertices. -/
theorem specModSig_le_card : specModSig G ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  rw [specModSig_eq_card_components]
  exact Fintype.card_le_of_surjective _ (connectedComponentMk_surjective G)

/-- A graph is connected iff its spectral modular signature is `1`. -/
theorem connected_iff_specModSig_eq_one :
    G.Connected ↔ specModSig G = 1 := by
  rw [specModSig_eq_card_components, connected_iff,
    Fintype.card_eq_one_iff_nonempty_unique]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hpre, hV⟩
    haveI := hpre.subsingleton_connectedComponent
    have hc : Nonempty G.ConnectedComponent := ⟨G.connectedComponentMk hV.some⟩
    obtain ⟨c⟩ := hc
    exact ⟨{ default := c, uniq := fun a => Subsingleton.elim a c }⟩
  · rintro ⟨u⟩
    haveI : Subsingleton G.ConnectedComponent := inferInstance
    have hpre : G.Preconnected := by
      intro a b
      have h := Subsingleton.elim (G.connectedComponentMk a) (G.connectedComponentMk b)
      rwa [ConnectedComponent.eq] at h
    obtain ⟨v, _⟩ := connectedComponentMk_surjective G u.default
    exact ⟨hpre, ⟨v⟩⟩

/-- Isomorphic graphs have equal spectral modular signatures. -/
theorem specModSig_iso {W : Type*} [Fintype W] [DecidableEq W]
    {H : SimpleGraph W} [DecidableRel H.Adj] (e : G ≃g H) :
    specModSig G = specModSig H := by
  rw [specModSig_eq_card_components, specModSig_eq_card_components,
    Fintype.card_congr e.connectedComponentEquiv]

/-- The signature attains its maximum `Fintype.card V` iff the graph is edgeless. -/
theorem specModSig_eq_card_iff_edgeless :
    specModSig G = Fintype.card V ↔ G = ⊥ := by
  rw [specModSig_eq_card_components]
  constructor
  · intro hcard
    have hbij : Function.Bijective G.connectedComponentMk :=
      (Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card _).2
        ⟨connectedComponentMk_surjective G, hcard.symm⟩
    ext u v
    rw [bot_adj]
    constructor
    · intro h
      exact (G.ne_of_adj h
        (hbij.1 (ConnectedComponent.connectedComponentMk_eq_of_adj h))).elim
    · intro h; exact h.elim
  · rintro rfl
    have hinj : Function.Injective (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).connectedComponentMk := by
      intro u v h
      rw [ConnectedComponent.eq, reachable_bot] at h
      exact h
    have hbij : Function.Bijective (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).connectedComponentMk :=
      ⟨hinj, connectedComponentMk_surjective _⟩
    exact ((Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card _).1 hbij).2.symm

end SpectralProofSignature

# Local arithmetic framework for the sequence `n² + 1`

This file develops, fully unconditionally and by elementary methods, the *local*
arithmetic ingredients attached to the polynomial sequence `n ↦ n² + 1`.  These
are the verifiable foundation stones underlying any (heuristic) sieve treatment
of the primes of the form `n² + 1`.  Nothing here depends on unproven sieve
machinery; everything is reduced to Mathlib's formalisation of quadratic
reciprocity and the theory of the Legendre symbol.

## Main results

* `LocalNSqPlusOne.solvable_iff` : for a prime `p`, the congruence
  `x² + 1 ≡ 0 (mod p)` is solvable in `ZMod p` iff `p % 4 ≠ 3`.
* `LocalNSqPlusOne.card_roots_eq_legendre` : the number of roots of `x² + 1` in
  `ZMod p` (for odd `p`) equals `legendreSym p (-1) + 1`.
* `LocalNSqPlusOne.localSolCount_one_mod_four` /
  `LocalNSqPlusOne.localSolCount_three_mod_four` /
  `LocalNSqPlusOne.localSolCount_two` : the exact solution counts
  (`2`, `0`, and `1` respectively).
* `LocalNSqPlusOne.localFactor_*` : the singular-series local density factors
  `ν_p / p` in closed form.
* `LocalNSqPlusOne.prime_dvd_sq_add_one` : every prime divisor `p` of `n² + 1`
  satisfies `p % 4 ≠ 3` (i.e. `p = 2` or `p ≡ 1 [MOD 4]`).
* `LocalNSqPlusOne.no_three_mod_four_factor` and
  `LocalNSqPlusOne.proportion_three_mod_four_zero` : consequently the set of
  `n ≤ X` for which `n² + 1` has a prime factor `≡ 3 (mod 4)` is **empty**, so
  the proportion in question is identically `0`.

## A remark on the singular series

The full *global* singular series `S = ∏_p ν_p / p` and the heuristic main term
`C · X / √(log X)` for the count of primes `n² + 1` lie beyond elementary
methods (they are equivalent to deep, still partly conjectural, analytic input).
We do **not** assert them as theorems.  What we formalise here are the exact
local factors `ν_p / p` entering that product; these are the rigorous,
unconditional ingredients.
-/

open scoped Classical

namespace LocalNSqPlusOne

/-! ## Part 1 — the local solvability criterion -/

/-- **Local solvability criterion.**  For a prime `p`, the congruence
`x² + 1 ≡ 0 (mod p)` has a solution in `ZMod p` if and only if `p % 4 ≠ 3`.
(For `p = 2` we have `2 % 4 = 2 ≠ 3`, and indeed `x = 1` is a solution.) -/
theorem solvable_iff (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    (∃ x : ZMod p, x ^ 2 + 1 = 0) ↔ p % 4 ≠ 3 := by
  rw [← ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff (p := p)]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    exact ⟨x, by rw [sq] at hx; linear_combination -hx⟩
  · rintro ⟨r, hr⟩
    exact ⟨r, by rw [sq]; linear_combination -hr⟩

/-- The Legendre-symbol value `(-1 / p) = 1` for `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`. -/
theorem legendre_neg_one_one_mod_four (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (h1 : p % 4 = 1) : legendreSym p (-1) = 1 := by
  rw [legendreSym.at_neg_one hp, ZMod.χ₄_nat_eq_if_mod_four]; split_ifs <;> omega

/-- The Legendre-symbol value `(-1 / p) = -1` for `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`. -/
theorem legendre_neg_one_three_mod_four (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (h3 : p % 4 = 3) : legendreSym p (-1) = -1 := by
  rw [legendreSym.at_neg_one hp, ZMod.χ₄_nat_eq_if_mod_four]; split_ifs <;> omega

/-! ## Part 2 — the exact number of solutions and the local density factors -/

/-- The local solution count `ν_p = #{x (mod p) : x² + 1 ≡ 0 (mod p)}`. -/
noncomputable def localSolCount (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : ZMod p => x ^ 2 + 1 = 0)).card

/-- Rewriting the set of roots of `x² + 1` as the set of square roots of `-1`. -/
private theorem roots_set_eq (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    {x : ZMod p | x ^ 2 = ((-1 : ℤ) : ZMod p)}.toFinset
      = Finset.univ.filter (fun x : ZMod p => x ^ 2 + 1 = 0) := by
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_toFinset, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
  push_cast
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linear_combination h

/-- For an odd prime `p`, the number of roots of `x² + 1` in `ZMod p` equals
`legendreSym p (-1) + 1`.  This is the special case `a = -1` of the general
formula counting square roots modulo `p`. -/
theorem card_roots_eq_legendre (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2) :
    (localSolCount p : ℤ) = legendreSym p (-1) + 1 := by
  unfold localSolCount
  have hcard := legendreSym.card_sqrts p hp (-1)
  rw [roots_set_eq p] at hcard
  exact hcard

/-- **Exactly two solutions** when `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`. -/
theorem localSolCount_one_mod_four (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (h1 : p % 4 = 1) : localSolCount p = 2 := by
  have h := card_roots_eq_legendre p hp
  rw [legendre_neg_one_one_mod_four p hp h1] at h
  have : (localSolCount p : ℤ) = 2 := by rw [h]; ring
  exact_mod_cast this

/-- **No solutions** when `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`. -/
theorem localSolCount_three_mod_four (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (h3 : p % 4 = 3) : localSolCount p = 0 := by
  have h := card_roots_eq_legendre p hp
  rw [legendre_neg_one_three_mod_four p hp h3] at h
  have : (localSolCount p : ℤ) = 0 := by rw [h]; ring
  exact_mod_cast this

/-- **One solution** at the prime `p = 2` (namely `x = 1`). -/
theorem localSolCount_two : localSolCount 2 = 1 := by
  haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 2) := ⟨Nat.prime_two⟩
  unfold localSolCount; decide

/-- The singular-series **local density factor** `ν_p / p`. -/
noncomputable def localFactor (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ℚ := (localSolCount p : ℚ) / p

/-- Closed form of the local factor at primes `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`: `ν_p / p = 2 / p`. -/
theorem localFactor_one_mod_four (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (h1 : p % 4 = 1) : localFactor p = 2 / p := by
  unfold localFactor; rw [localSolCount_one_mod_four p hp h1]; norm_num

/-- Closed form of the local factor at primes `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`: `ν_p / p = 0`. -/
theorem localFactor_three_mod_four (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hp : p ≠ 2)
    (h3 : p % 4 = 3) : localFactor p = 0 := by
  unfold localFactor; rw [localSolCount_three_mod_four p hp h3]; norm_num

integer `n`) satisfies `p % 4 ≠ 3`; equivalently `p = 2` or `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`.
This is the unconditional reason the sieve has no "bad" local obstructions at
primes `≡ 3 (mod 4)`. -/
theorem prime_dvd_sq_add_one (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (n : ℤ)
    (h : (p : ℤ) ∣ n ^ 2 + 1) : p % 4 ≠ 3 := by
  haveI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩
  rw [← ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff (p := p)]
  refine ⟨(n : ZMod p), ?_⟩
  have hz : ((n ^ 2 + 1 : ℤ) : ZMod p) = 0 := by
    rw [ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd]; exact_mod_cast h
  push_cast at hz
  linear_combination -hz

/-- Natural-number version of `prime_dvd_sq_add_one`. -/
theorem prime_dvd_sq_add_one_nat (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (n : ℕ)
    (h : p ∣ n ^ 2 + 1) : p % 4 ≠ 3 := by
  apply prime_dvd_sq_add_one p hp (n : ℤ)
  have : (p : ℤ) ∣ ((n ^ 2 + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast h
  push_cast at this ⊢
  exact this

/-- An odd prime divisor of `n² + 1` is necessarily `≡ 1 (mod 4)`. -/
theorem odd_prime_dvd_sq_add_one (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hodd : p ≠ 2) (n : ℤ)
    (h : (p : ℤ) ∣ n ^ 2 + 1) : p % 4 = 1 := by
  have hne3 := prime_dvd_sq_add_one p hp n h
  have h2 : p % 2 = 1 := hp.eq_two_or_odd.resolve_left hodd

      (fun n => ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p % 4 = 3 ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ (n : ℤ) ^ 2 + 1)) = ∅ := by
  rw [Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
  intro n _
  exact no_three_mod_four_factor (n : ℤ)

**Local densities / singular series.** For the sequence `n²+1`, the sieve and the
circle method both sum over the *local data* `ρ(p)` = number of roots of `x²+1`

# Future Directions — Primes of the Form n² + 1

Derived from the Stage 3 analysis and Stage 4 critique of this research cycle.
Each conjecture is bold and falsifiable, with the decisive insight and a "why
now?" justification. Statuses refer to the formal artifacts in
`Cryptography/PrimesNSqPlusOne.lean` and `Cryptography/SqAddOneDivisors.lean`.

## C1. Quantitative divisor-density of the n²+1 sequence

**Conjecture.** For every `X`, the number of *distinct* primes `≡ 1 (mod 4)`
dividing some `n² + 1` with `n ≤ X` grows at least like `c · X / log X`.

The key insight is that the converse `oddPrime_dvd_some_sq_add_one` already gives
a *root* `n < p` for each such prime, so a counting argument over the box
`n ≤ X` should recover a positive proportion of all `1 mod 4` primes up to `X²`.

Why now? We have the exact "which primes occur" characterization
(`oddPrime_dvd_sq_add_one_iff`) formalized; turning the qualitative `Set.Infinite`
result into a density statement is the natural next quantitative step and needs
only counting infrastructure already in Mathlib.

## C2. Parity-refined Landau bases

**Conjecture.** Apart from `n = 1`, every base `n` with `n² + 1` prime is
divisible by `2` but the quotient `n/2` is *not* forced into any single residue
class mod 4 — i.e. `landau_base_even` is the *only* unconditional congruence
obstruction on the base.

The key insight is that `landau_base_even` is proved purely from the evenness of
`n² + 1` for odd `n`; any further base obstruction would have to come from a
prime `≡ 3 (mod 4)` dividing `n² + 1`, which `oddPrime_dvd_sq_add_one_mod_four`
forbids — suggesting no further constraint exists.

Why now? The minimal-obstruction principle is fully formal on the divisor side;
proving the base side has *no* extra constraint is a clean, testable target
(falsifiable by a single counter-pattern in a finite search).

## C3. Iwaniec P₂ lower bound via the formal sieve skeleton

**Conjecture.** The count of `n ≤ X` with `IsSemiprimeValue n`
(`n²+1` a product of ≤ 2 primes) is `≫ X / log X`.

The key insight is that the same congruence filter that excludes `3 mod 4` prime
factors (`three_not_dvd_sq_add_one`) is exactly the local condition feeding
Iwaniec's half-dimensional sieve; formalizing the sieve's *combinatorial*
skeleton (Buchstab/Selmer weights) is separable from the analytic bound.

Why now? `IsSemiprimeValue` is already defined; a Lean development of the
linear/half-dimensional sieve would unlock this and many neighboring results,
and Mathlib's analytic number theory is mature enough to host it.

## C4. Friedlander–Iwaniec strictly enlarges the Landau form

**Conjecture.** The inclusion `{Landau primes} ⊆ {a²+b⁴ primes}`
(`landauPrime_isFIPrime`) is *strict*: there are infinitely many `a²+b⁴` primes
that are **not** of the form `n² + 1`.

The key insight is that fixing `b = 1` collapses `a²+b⁴` to `a²+1`, so any prime
of the form `a² + b⁴` with `b ≥ 2` (e.g. `a²+16`) that is not a perfect-square
shift witnesses strictness; the Friedlander–Iwaniec count `X^{3/4}` dwarfs the
conjectured Landau count `X^{1/2}/log X`.

Why now? The set inclusion is formalized; quantifying the gap between the two
exponents is a concrete, falsifiable density separation.

## C5. Gaussian-integer bridge to cryptographic splitting primes

**Conjecture.** A prime `p` is usable as a "split modulus prime" for
`ℤ[i]`-based key agreement (i.e. `p` splits in `ℤ[i]`) **iff** `p` divides some
`n² + 1`, and this set has natural density `1/2` among all primes.

The key insight is `oddPrime_dvd_sq_add_one_iff`: divisibility of `n²+1` is
*equivalent* to `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, which is exactly the Gaussian-splitting
condition — directly tying the number theory to the cryptographic domain of this
catalog.

Why now? The iff is verified here; combining it with Dirichlet density
(`Nat.infinite_setOf_prime_modEq_one` and its quantitative refinements) makes the
`1/2`-density claim a near-term formalization target.
